controls.name: Mandatory reporting to government
controls.definition: Requires developers or deployers to report, disclose, register, or submit safety plans, incidents, audits, or impact assessments to a government body, or to produce them on government demand.

controls.name: Labels and watermarks on AI content
controls.definition: Requires labels, watermarks, provenance data, or disclosures on AI-generated content or AI interactions.

controls.name: Moratoriums and limits on data centers
controls.definition: Pauses, bans, or adds new permitting restrictions or special conditions on building or operating data centers.

controls.name: New powers for government agencies
controls.definition: Creates a new government office or agency for AI, or gives an existing agency or attorney general new rulemaking, oversight, or enforcement authority over AI.

controls.name: ID and age checks for users
controls.definition: Requires identity verification, age verification, or know-your-customer checks for users, customers, or buyers of AI services or compute.

controls.name: Licenses required to build AI
controls.definition: Requires a license, registration, certification, or government permission before developing, training, or deploying an AI system or model.

controls.name: Export controls on models and chips
controls.definition: Restricts exports or foreign access to AI chips, models, compute, or AI technology.

controls.name: State laws overridden by Washington
controls.definition: Overrides, preempts, or blocks state or local AI laws, or conditions funding on states not regulating AI.

controls.name: Caps on who can train models
controls.definition: Sets compute, cost, or capability thresholds that trigger restrictions or obligations on who may train or release large AI models.

controls.name: Limits on sharing open models
controls.definition: Restricts publishing, sharing, or open-sourcing AI model weights or code.
